title: Introducing Strands Agents, an Open Source AI Agents SDK — Suman Debnath, AWS

summary: The presentation introduces Strands Agents, an open-source SDK from AWS that simplifies AI agent creation by eliminating complex orchestration and scaffolding. The core philosophy is model-driven: a model, an optional system prompt, and a set of tools are all that's needed. The SDK relies on modern foundation models to handle reasoning, tool use, and reflection autonomously, rather than requiring developers to script agent behavior through extensive prompts. The Strands logo symbolically represents two strands: one for the model, one for tools. Strands integrates with third-party providers including Langfuse and LiteLLM, allowing users to select any model—including locally hosted ones via Ollama—rather than being locked to AWS Bedrock. By default, the SDK uses Bedrock with Claude 3.7. The first demonstration shows a simple agent built with three default tools (read file, write file, speak) installed via pip from strands-tools. The agent reads a chapter file, generates a summary, writes it to markdown, and speaks the result aloud—all in just a few lines of code with no custom tool development required. The system prompt is optional; the agent works without it. The second demonstration highlights MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration, building a Strands agent that connects to an MCP server running manim (the library behind 3Blue1Brown-style mathematical animations). The MCP client's tools are broadcast to the agent via list_tools_sync, enabling the agent to generate visualization videos for mathematical concepts like cubic equations, SVD, or byte-pair encoding without any scaffolding prompts. Custom tools are created by importing the tool decorator from Strands and wrapping any Python function, which then becomes available alongside default tools when creating an agent. Resources include the launch blog, documentation at strandsagent.com, and the GitHub repository. The project is open source and welcomes community contributions via PRs.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction to Strands SDK
sections.summary: Overview of Strands as an open-source SDK with a model-driven philosophy requiring only model and tools without scaffolding. Integrations with Langfuse, LiteLLM, and Ollama are mentioned. The Strands logo represents two strands: one for model, one for tool.

sections.title: Demo 1 — File Operations with Default Tools
sections.summary: Live demo of installing Strands via pip, creating an agent with default tools (read file, write file, speak) that reads chapter 10, summarizes it, writes to markdown, and speaks the result. Shows model definition options (Bedrock default, Ollama alternative) and optional system prompt.

sections.title: Demo 2 — MCP Integration with Manim
sections.summary: Demo of a Strands agent connected to an MCP server for generating 3Blue1Brown-style mathematical animations using manim. Shows MCP client setup, tool broadcasting via list_tools_sync, and generation of a cubic equation visualization. No scaffolding prompts provided to the agent.

sections.title: MCP Server Code and Custom Tools
sections.summary: Walkthrough of MCP server code using FastMCP with decorator-based tool definitions. Demonstrates custom tool creation by wrapping Python functions with Strands' @tool decorator. Shows one-shot prompting examples for manim and an interactive chat loop.

sections.title: Resources and Closing
sections.summary: Resources shared: launch blog, documentation at strandsagent.com, and GitHub repository. The open source project welcomes PRs and community contributions. Booth available with additional demos.

demonstrations: Demo 1: Agent reads a file, summarizes it, writes to markdown, and speaks the result using default Strands tools (read file, write file, speak)
Demo 2: Agent connected to MCP server generates manim-based mathematical animation videos (e.g., cubic equation visualization within range x=-3 to x=3)
Custom tool creation by decorating Python functions with Strands' @tool decorator
